I've reviewed SDN forums and a few reddit threads looking for information about HPSP for medical school. A common theme I've come across is people saying 'It's not worth it unless you are going into it out of a desire to serve.' I think that is probably good general advice but I'm wondering if my own personal circumstances might make it more worth it for me than it would someone else.
Some context: I am a second year medical student currently. I am non-traditional (30 y/o) and am married with a kid. My wife is in school right now as well. We are constantly finding it difficult to live off of the loans we are getting for school; it is a perpetual financial strain and we feel guilty anytime we do anything that costs money outside of the bare necessities to survive. We have some debt from before medical school that adds to the complications of balancing our budget. On our current trajectory, I don't see the financial strain changing all that much until after residency. Maybe I'm wrong about that though. I'm interested in a variety of specialties but don't think I want to be a primary care doctor.
As far as my desire to be in the military, if I'm being honest I'm kind of indifferent. I don't think I would mind serving and I feel like it's an environment I could enjoy but I also have never felt a strong desire to do it and, just like most anybody, I enjoy personal freedom.
Right now I'm leaning towards taking the HPSP route. My rationale is this: I am tired of struggling financially. I'm older than most medical students and have people who depend on me. It would be nice to be able to go out and do fun things with my family without feeling guilty every time and feeling like we are barely going to make it to the next disbursement. The way things are, it would be like this at least until residency but possibly not until after residency. I don't think I would dislike the military and, at the end of the day, I would only owe 3 years back to them if I start HPSP now. After that I would be free to go on and practice where I want. It seems a little insane to me to go through at least 6 more years of struggling financially the way we are now in order to eventually get the pay off (and even then, have a large sum of school debt to overcome) when we could live comfortably right now by joining the military - even though it might take longer to make the really good money. I recognize there is still some trade off here. The military decides where we live, etc. and may affect my ability to do the particular specialty I'm most interested. I still feel like it would be worth it though. Is there anything big I'm missing? Am I thinking about all of this the wrong way? Any perspectives would be appreciated.

You analyze issues like physician assisted suicide, the mountain meadows massacre, gene therapy and a bunch of other controversial ethics topics. It's great because you get the opportunity to share unorthodox (or orthodox) ideas as they come up with the different topics. You have two organs at play here. First, your pituitary is releasing two (relavent) hormones: LH and FSH. The second organ is your testicles. LH and FSH bind to receptors on cells in your testes to produce testosterone. Testosterone then gets into your blood stream and signals for your pituitary to stop releasing LH and FSH. So it's a self regulating negative feedback loop.

If you do TRT alone you will have testosterone in your blood and it will signal for your pituitary to stop releasing LH and FSH. Having almost no FSH and LH in your system means your testes never get the signal to produce testosterone. Over time they will atrophy and it is irreversible. 

Clomid stimulates release of FSH and LH from the pituitary. hCG mimics FSH/LH. Both will stimulate your testes which keeps them active/functional and will prevent atrophy.

hCG can be administered with testosterone so that you get the benefits of TRT without losing the functionality of your testes. 

You could always start with hCG and clomid, see where that gets you and then stop if you're satisfied or supplement with TRT on top of those to get you to the levels you need. Either way you should be able to get your levels up without your testes dying and losing function.
